objects.definition: typedef struct JSRuntime JSRuntime;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a QuickJS runtime. Only forward-declared here; definition is hidden. Lifetime managed by JS_NewRuntime/JS_FreeRuntime.

objects.definition: typedef struct JSContext JSContext;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a QuickJS context (execution context within a runtime). Forward-declared only.

objects.definition: typedef struct JSClass JSClass;
objects.description: Opaque internal class metadata structure. Only forward-declared.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t JSClassID;
objects.description: 32-bit identifier for a registered JS class. Values are allocated via JS_NewClassID and used with class APIs.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t JSAtom;
objects.description: Atom table index representing interned strings/symbols in QuickJS.
Header embedded in ref-counted QuickJS heap objects. Used for manual refcount mgmt of JSValue payloads.
Storage union for non-NaN-boxed builds holding number, pointer, or short big int representations for JSValue.
Tagged JavaScript value representation. Exact layout depends on configuration (NaN boxing vs struct). Use API functions/macros to manipulate.
State passed to custom memory functions for tracking allocations and user data.
Function table to customize allocation for a runtime.

objects.definition: typedef struct JSGCObjectHeader JSGCObjectHeader;
objects.description: Opaque header used by the GC for heap objects.
Aggregated memory accounting snapshot for a runtime.
Describes a property key discovered during enumeration, with its enumerability flag and atom id.
Descriptor used to query or define object properties, holding flags, value, and accessor functions.
Optional virtual methods to customize fundamental object behaviors for a class.

objects.definition: typedef void JSClassFinalizer(JSRuntime *rt, JSValue val);
objects.description: Callback invoked when an object of a given class is garbage collected to release resources.

objects.definition:
typedef void JSClassGCMark(JSRuntime *rt, JSValueConst val,
                           JS_MarkFunc *mark_func);
objects.description: Callback to mark child GC references of an object during GC tracing.
Call handler for function objects of a class (constructor or normal call).
Definition record used to register a class: name, lifecycle callbacks, call handler, and optional exotic methods.

objects.definition: typedef void JSFreeArrayBufferDataFunc(JSRuntime *rt, void *opaque, void *ptr);
objects.description: Finalizer for external ArrayBuffer data to release native memory when detached/freed.

typedef enum JSTypedArrayEnum {

objects.description: Enumeration of typed array element types supported by QuickJS.
Callbacks to integrate host-managed SharedArrayBuffer backing store allocation and lifetime.
Promise state values returned by JS_PromiseState.
Host callback notified when a promise is rejected or handled.

objects.definition: typedef int JSInterruptHandler(JSRuntime *rt, void *opaque);
objects.description: Host callback polled to interrupt JS execution; return non-zero to interrupt.

objects.definition: typedef struct JSModuleDef JSModuleDef;
objects.description: Opaque module definition object used for ES modules and C modules.
Host callback to normalize a module specifier to a canonical name.

objects.definition:
typedef JSModuleDef *JSModuleLoaderFunc(JSContext *ctx,
                                        const char *module_name, void *opaque);
objects.description: Host callback to load a module by name without attributes.
Host callback to load a module by name with import attributes.

objects.definition:
typedef int JSModuleCheckSupportedImportAttributes(JSContext *ctx, void *opaque,
                                                   JSValueConst attributes);
objects.description: Host callback to validate import attributes used with a loader.

objects.definition: typedef JSValue JSJobFunc(JSContext *ctx, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
objects.description: Job function signature scheduled on the microtask queue.

objects.description: Discriminator for different C function signatures that can be exposed as JS functions.
Union of possible C callable function pointer types for JS function bindings.
Descriptor used to define properties, functions, getters/setters, constants, and nested definitions on JS objects.

objects.definition: typedef int JSModuleInitFunc(JSContext *ctx, JSModuleDef *m);
objects.description: Initialization callback for a C module to define its exports.
Options controlling pretty-printing of JS values for debugging/logging.

objects.definition: typedef void JSPrintValueWrite(void *opaque, const char *buf, size_t len);
objects.description: Write callback used by debugging print routines to emit text.

objects.definition: typedef void JS_MarkFunc(JSRuntime *rt, JSGCObjectHeader *gp);
objects.description: Tracer callback used during GC marking to visit references from host objects.
Function pointer types for C callbacks exposed to JS as functions, with variants carrying magic numbers or bound data.
Host hook for resolving module specifiers to canonical names.

functions.name: JS_NewRuntime
functions.description: Create a new QuickJS runtime (heap/GC/atoms shared across contexts). Use as the top-level owner for subsequent contexts.
requirements: Must be paired with JS_FreeRuntime(rt) when no longer needed.
Returns NULL on failure (out of memory); caller must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: JS_SetRuntimeInfo
functions.description: Attach an informational string to the runtime (lifetime of info must exceed rt).
requirements: rt must be a valid JSRuntime* created by JS_NewRuntime/JS_NewRuntime2.
The comment states: info lifetime must exceed that of rt; caller must keep info string alive until after JS_FreeRuntime.

functions.name: JS_SetMemoryLimit
functions.description: Set a soft memory usage limit for the runtime.
requirements: limit is in bytes; 0 means no explicit limit (inferred).

functions.name: JS_SetGCThreshold
functions.description: Configure the runtime’s GC threshold which influences when GC runs.
requirements: gc_threshold is in bytes (inferred from naming); must be a reasonable positive size.

functions.name: JS_SetMaxStackSize
functions.description: Set the maximum stack size used for stack overflow checks. Use 0 to disable the maximum stack size check.
requirements: stack_size of 0 disables the check; otherwise should reflect the host thread’s actual limit.

functions.name: JS_UpdateStackTop
functions.description: Update the runtime’s notion of the current thread’s stack top after a thread change to keep stack overflow checks accurate.
requirements: Must be called when changing thread associated with the runtime (as noted in comment).

functions.name: JS_NewRuntime2
functions.description: Create a new runtime using custom allocator callbacks and an allocator opaque value.
requirements: mf may be NULL to use defaults (not stated; if provided, all function pointers should be valid).
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check.
Opaque is stored in the allocator state and retrievable by callbacks.

functions.name: JS_FreeRuntime
functions.description: Destroy a runtime and free all associated resources (contexts, values, atoms, GC objects).
requirements: rt must have been created by JS_NewRuntime/JS_NewRuntime2.
All JSContext objects created from rt must be freed before or by freeing the runtime (QuickJS typically allows freeing contexts after runtime but recommended to free contexts first).
Do not use rt after this call.

functions.name: JS_GetRuntimeOpaque
functions.description: Get the user-defined opaque pointer stored on the runtime.

functions.name: JS_SetRuntimeOpaque
functions.description: Associate a user-defined opaque pointer with the runtime for host use.
requirements: No ownership transfer implied; caller manages the lifetime of opaque.

functions.name: JS_MarkValue
functions.description: Mark a JS value during GC tracing using a custom mark function for embedding custom GC-managed data.
requirements: mark_func must be a function compatible with JS_MarkFunc; may be NULL only if not needed (unspecified).
Typically called during host GC integration/mark phases.

functions.name: JS_RunGC
functions.description: Force a garbage collection cycle for the runtime.

functions.name: JS_IsLiveObject
functions.description: Check if a JS object value is considered live (not collected) within the runtime.
requirements: obj should be a JS object value; if not an object, the result is unspecified (inferred).

functions.name: JS_NewContext
functions.description: Create a new JS execution context tied to the runtime with standard intrinsics enabled.
requirements: rt must be a valid JSRuntime*.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_FreeContext
functions.description: Destroy a JS context and free associated resources owned by the context.
requirements: s must be a context created by JS_NewContext/JS_NewContextRaw.
All JSValue instances referencing context-owned resources should be released before freeing the context to avoid leaks.
Do not use s after this call.

functions.name: JS_DupContext
functions.description: Increment the reference count of a context and return it (duplicate reference).
requirements: Caller must later balance with JS_FreeContext when done.

functions.name: JS_GetContextOpaque
functions.description: Get the user-defined opaque pointer stored on a context.

functions.name: JS_SetContextOpaque
functions.description: Associate a user-defined opaque pointer with a context.
requirements: No ownership transfer implied; caller manages lifetime of opaque.

functions.name: JS_GetRuntime
functions.description: Return the runtime owning the given context.

functions.name: JS_SetClassProto
functions.signature: void JS_SetClassProto(JSContext *ctx, JSClassID class_id, JSValue obj);
functions.description: Set the default prototype object for a given class ID in the context.
requirements: obj must be a JS object or null; ownership of obj is transferred to the engine (value is consumed).
class_id must be a valid class ID (created/registered).

functions.name: JS_GetClassProto
functions.description: Get the default prototype object for a given class ID. Returns a JSValue that must be freed if it has ref-count.
requirements: On failure or if not found, may return JS_NULL or JS_EXCEPTION; caller must check JS_IsException.
If the returned value has a reference (object), follow normal JSValue lifetime and call JS_FreeValue(ctx, v) when done.

functions.name: JS_NewContextRaw
functions.description: Create a new JS context with minimal built-in intrinsics; caller must add desired intrinsic objects via JS_AddIntrinsic* functions.
requirements: Returns NULL on failure; caller must check.
After creation, typically call JS_AddIntrinsic* before executing scripts.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicBaseObjects
functions.description: Install base intrinsic objects (Object, Function, etc.) into a raw context to save memory when customizing environments.
requirements: Returns 0 on success, -1 on exception; caller must check and handle exceptions via JS_GetException.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicDate
functions.description: Add the Date intrinsic into a raw context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicEval
functions.description: Add eval-related intrinsics into a raw context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicStringNormalize
functions.description: Add String.prototype.normalize (Unicode normalization) into a raw context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicRegExpCompiler
functions.description: Add RegExp compiler support into a raw context (internal helper; void return).

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicRegExp
functions.description: Add RegExp intrinsics into a raw context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicJSON
functions.description: Add JSON intrinsics into a raw context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicProxy
functions.description: Add Proxy intrinsics into a raw context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicMapSet
functions.description: Add Map and Set intrinsics into a raw context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicTypedArrays
functions.description: Add TypedArray and ArrayBuffer/DataView intrinsics into a raw context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicPromise
functions.description: Add Promise intrinsic into a raw context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicWeakRef
functions.description: Add WeakRef and related intrinsics into a raw context.

functions.name: js_string_codePointRange
functions.signature: JSValue js_string_codePointRange(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_val, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: An exposed helper to compute or validate a string code point range (exact semantics not documented; inferred by name).
requirements: On error returns JS_EXCEPTION; caller must check.
argv must have at most argc elements; contents should be JS strings or numbers as expected by this function (unknown specifics).

functions.name: js_malloc_rt
functions.description: Allocate memory tied to the runtime’s allocator.
requirements: Returns NULL on allocation failure; caller must check.
Memory must be freed with js_free_rt(rt, ptr).

functions.name: js_free_rt
functions.description: Free memory previously allocated with js_malloc_rt/js_realloc_rt for the same runtime.
requirements: Pointer must originate from the same runtime’s allocator.

functions.name: js_realloc_rt
functions.description: Reallocate memory using the runtime’s allocator.
requirements: ptr may be NULL to behave like malloc.
Returns NULL on failure; on failure original ptr remains valid and unchanged.
Result must be freed with js_free_rt(rt, new_ptr).

functions.name: js_malloc_usable_size_rt
functions.description: Return the usable size of an allocation made by the runtime allocator.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer returned by js_malloc_rt/js_realloc_rt.

functions.name: js_mallocz_rt
functions.description: Allocate zero-initialized memory with the runtime allocator.
requirements: Returns NULL on failure; caller must check.

functions.name: js_malloc
functions.description: Allocate memory using the context’s allocator.
requirements: Returns NULL on failure; caller must check.

functions.name: js_free
functions.description: Free memory allocated by js_malloc/js_realloc for the same context.
requirements: Pointer must originate from the same context allocator.

functions.name: js_realloc
functions.description: Reallocate memory using the context allocator.
requirements: ptr may be NULL to behave like malloc.
Returns NULL on failure; original ptr remains valid.

functions.name: js_malloc_usable_size
functions.description: Return the usable size of an allocation made by the context allocator.
requirements: ptr must come from js_malloc/js_realloc for this context.

functions.name: js_realloc2
functions.description: Reallocate with context allocator and optionally report slack/extra usable size via pslack.
requirements: ptr may be NULL to behave like malloc.
pslack may be NULL if slack not needed.
Returns NULL on failure; original ptr remains valid.

functions.name: js_mallocz
functions.description: Allocate zero-initialized memory with the context allocator.
requirements: Returns NULL on failure; caller must check.

functions.name: js_strdup
functions.description: Duplicate a C string using the context allocator.
requirements: str must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
Returns NULL on failure; free with js_free(ctx, ptr).

functions.name: js_strndup
functions.description: Duplicate up to n bytes of a C string using the context allocator, NUL-terminating the result.
requirements: Returns NULL on failure; free with js_free(ctx, ptr).

functions.name: JS_ComputeMemoryUsage
functions.description: Populate a JSMemoryUsage struct with detailed memory statistics for the runtime.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to writable struct.

functions.name: JS_DumpMemoryUsage
functions.description: Print formatted memory usage statistics to a FILE* for the provided snapshot and runtime.
requirements: fp must be a valid writable FILE*.
s must point to previously filled memory usage data (e.g., by JS_ComputeMemoryUsage).

functions.name: JS_NewAtomLen
functions.signature: JSAtom JS_NewAtomLen(JSContext *ctx, const char *str, size_t len);
functions.description: Create or intern an atom from a byte string of given length.
requirements: The string bytes need not be NUL-terminated; only len bytes are considered.
Returns JS_ATOM_NULL (0) on failure; check and handle accordingly.

functions.name: JS_NewAtom
functions.description: Create or intern an atom from a NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: JS_NewAtomUInt32
functions.description: Create or intern an atom representing an array index/property key from an unsigned 32-bit integer.

functions.name: JS_DupAtom
functions.description: Increment the reference count of an atom and return it.
requirements: Atom v must be a valid (non-zero) atom previously obtained.
Must be later balanced with JS_FreeAtom(ctx, v).

functions.name: JS_FreeAtom
functions.description: Decrement the reference count of an atom in a context.
requirements: Atom v should be one previously obtained/duplicated; safe to call with 0 only if the API tolerates (not specified).

functions.name: JS_FreeAtomRT
functions.description: Decrement atom refcount at the runtime level.
requirements: v must be a valid atom.

functions.name: JS_AtomToValue
functions.description: Convert an atom to a JS string value.
requirements: Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.
Returned JSValue must be freed with JS_FreeValue(ctx, v) when no longer needed.

functions.name: JS_AtomToString
functions.description: Convert an atom to a JS string value (alias of JS_AtomToValue for strings).
requirements: Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.
Free returned value with JS_FreeValue(ctx, v).

functions.name: JS_AtomToCStringLen
functions.description: Return a UTF-8 C string for the given atom, optionally returning its byte length.
requirements: Returns NULL on error; caller must check.
The returned pointer must be freed with JS_FreeCString(ctx, ptr).

functions.name: JS_ValueToAtom
functions.description: Intern an atom from a JS value (typically string or symbol).
requirements: Returns JS_ATOM_NULL (0) on error; caller must check.
If successful, manage atom lifetime and free with JS_FreeAtom when done.

functions.name: JS_NewClassID
functions.description: Allocate a new unique class ID. If pclass_id is non-NULL, store it there and return it.
requirements: pclass_id may be NULL; when non-NULL must be writable.

functions.name: JS_GetClassID
functions.description: Return the class ID if v is an object; otherwise return JS_INVALID_CLASS_ID.

functions.name: JS_NewClass
functions.signature: int JS_NewClass(JSRuntime *rt, JSClassID class_id, const JSClassDef *class_def);
functions.description: Register a new class with the runtime (name, finalizer, call behavior, exotic methods).
requirements: class_id must be previously allocated (e.g., via JS_NewClassID).
class_def must point to a valid, fully initialized JSClassDef; its pointers must remain valid for the runtime’s lifetime (implied by typical pattern).

functions.name: JS_IsRegisteredClass
functions.description: Check whether a class ID is registered in the runtime.

functions.name: JS_NewBigInt64
functions.description: Create a new BigInt value from a signed 64-bit integer.
requirements: Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.
Free with JS_FreeValue(ctx, v) when done.

functions.name: JS_NewBigUint64
functions.description: Create a new BigInt value from an unsigned 64-bit integer.
requirements: Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_Throw
functions.description: Throw a JS exception object in the context and return JS_EXCEPTION. Transfers ownership of obj to the engine.
requirements: obj should be an Error object or any throwable JSValue; it is consumed by the engine and should not be freed by the caller afterwards.

functions.name: JS_SetUncatchableException
functions.description: Mark the current pending exception as uncatchable (or clear the mark).
requirements: There must be a pending exception for the flag to have effect (implied).

functions.name: JS_GetException
functions.description: Retrieve and clear the current pending exception from the context.
requirements: If no exception is pending, returns JS_NULL (typical) or an implementation-defined value; check docs by testing JS_IsException on operations instead.
Returned value must be freed with JS_FreeValue(ctx, v) when done.

functions.name: JS_HasException
functions.description: Return whether there is a pending exception in the context.

functions.name: JS_IsError
functions.description: Return whether the given value is an Error object.

functions.name: JS_NewError
functions.description: Create a new generic Error object.
requirements: Returns JS_EXCEPTION on failure; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_ThrowSyntaxError
functions.description: Format and throw a SyntaxError exception; returns JS_EXCEPTION. printf-like formatting.
requirements: fmt must be a valid format string with matching arguments.

functions.name: JS_ThrowTypeError
functions.description: Format and throw a TypeError exception; returns JS_EXCEPTION. printf-like formatting.
requirements: fmt must be valid; arguments must match format.

functions.name: JS_ThrowReferenceError
functions.description: Format and throw a ReferenceError exception; returns JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: fmt and varargs must be valid.

functions.name: JS_ThrowRangeError
functions.description: Format and throw a RangeError exception; returns JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: fmt and varargs must be valid.

functions.name: JS_ThrowInternalError
functions.description: Format and throw an InternalError exception; returns JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: fmt and varargs must be valid.

functions.name: JS_ThrowOutOfMemory
functions.description: Throw an out-of-memory exception and return JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: __JS_FreeValue
functions.description: Internal function to free a ref-counted JSValue (called when its refcount reaches zero).
requirements: Normally use JS_FreeValue instead of calling this directly.

functions.name: __JS_FreeValueRT
functions.description: Internal runtime-level free of a ref-counted JSValue.
requirements: Normally use JS_FreeValueRT instead of calling this directly.

functions.name: JS_StrictEq
functions.signature: JS_BOOL JS_StrictEq(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst op1, JSValueConst op2);
functions.description: Perform JavaScript strict equality comparison (===) between two values.
requirements: Returns -1 is not specified; API returns JS_BOOL (0/1).

functions.name: JS_SameValue
functions.signature: JS_BOOL JS_SameValue(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst op1, JSValueConst op2);
functions.description: Perform JavaScript SameValue comparison (like Object.is semantics).

functions.name: JS_SameValueZero
functions.signature: JS_BOOL JS_SameValueZero(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst op1, JSValueConst op2);
functions.description: Perform JavaScript SameValueZero comparison (NaN is equal to NaN; +0 and -0 are equal).

functions.name: JS_ToBool
functions.description: Convert a JS value to boolean; returns -1 on exception, otherwise 0 or 1.
requirements: Caller must handle return -1 as exception (use JS_GetException).

functions.name: JS_ToInt32
functions.description: Convert a JS value to a 32-bit signed integer.
requirements: pres must be a valid pointer.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on exception; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_ToInt64
functions.description: Convert a JS value to a 64-bit signed integer (Numbers only; BigInt not allowed).
requirements: pres must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: JS_ToIndex
functions.description: Convert a JS value to a valid index length (ToIndex operation).
requirements: plen must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: JS_ToFloat64
functions.description: Convert a JS value to a double.
requirements: pres must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: JS_ToBigInt64
functions.description: Convert a BigInt JS value to a signed 64-bit integer; returns an exception if val is a Number.
requirements: pres must be a valid pointer.
val must be a BigInt; if not, conversion fails with exception.

functions.name: JS_ToInt64Ext
functions.description: Convert a JS value to a 64-bit integer, accepting both Number and BigInt inputs.
requirements: pres must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: JS_NewStringLen
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewStringLen(JSContext *ctx, const char *str1, size_t len1);
functions.description: Create a new JS string from len1 bytes of str1 (may contain NULs).
requirements: str1 may be NULL only if len1 is zero (typical C pattern; not specified).
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.
Free resulting JSValue with JS_FreeValue(ctx, v).

functions.name: JS_NewAtomString
functions.description: Create a new JS string that is interned/atomized from a C string.
requirements: Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_ToString
functions.description: Convert a JS value to a JS string (ToString).
requirements: Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.
Free returned string with JS_FreeValue(ctx, v).

functions.name: JS_ToPropertyKey
functions.description: Convert a JS value to a property key (string or symbol).
requirements: Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.
Free returned value with JS_FreeValue(ctx, v).

functions.name: JS_ToCStringLen2
functions.signature: const char *JS_ToCStringLen2(JSContext *ctx, size_t *plen, JSValueConst val1, JS_BOOL cesu8);
functions.description: Convert a JS value to a newly allocated const char* UTF-8 (or CESU-8 if cesu8) string; optionally return its byte length.
requirements: Returns NULL on error; caller must check.
The returned pointer must be freed with JS_FreeCString(ctx, ptr).

functions.name: JS_FreeCString
functions.description: Free a C string buffer returned by JS_ToCString*/JS_AtomToCStringLen.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer returned by a QuickJS string conversion for the same context; may be NULL (no-op).

functions.name: JS_NewObjectProtoClass
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewObjectProtoClass(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst proto, JSClassID class_id);
functions.description: Create a new object with the given prototype and class ID.
requirements: proto should be an object or JS_NULL.
class_id must be a registered class ID.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.
Free created object with JS_FreeValue(ctx, v) when done or let GC collect it.

functions.name: JS_NewObjectClass
functions.description: Create a new object with the given class ID and default prototype.
requirements: class_id must be a registered class ID.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; check and free appropriately.

functions.name: JS_NewObjectProto
functions.description: Create a new plain object with the provided prototype.
requirements: proto should be object or JS_NULL.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_NewObject
functions.description: Create a new plain object with the standard Object prototype.
requirements: Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_IsFunction
functions.description: Test whether a value is a callable JS function object.

functions.name: JS_IsConstructor
functions.description: Test whether a value is a constructor function (has [[Construct]]).

functions.name: JS_SetConstructorBit
functions.signature: JS_BOOL JS_SetConstructorBit(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst func_obj, JS_BOOL val);
functions.description: Set or clear the internal flag marking an object as a constructor-capable function.
requirements: func_obj should be a function object; otherwise behavior may be undefined.
Returns non-zero on success; 0 or negative on failure (unspecified).

functions.name: JS_NewArray
functions.description: Create a new JS Array object.
requirements: Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_IsArray
functions.description: Determine whether a value is a JS Array (1 yes, 0 no, <0 exception).
requirements: Caller must handle negative return as exception.

functions.name: JS_NewDate
functions.description: Create a new JS Date object from milliseconds since the epoch.
requirements: Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_GetPropertyInternal
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetPropertyInternal(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, JSAtom prop, JSValueConst receiver, JS_BOOL throw_ref_error);
functions.description: Low-level property getter with explicit receiver and option to throw on reference error.
requirements: obj must be an object value.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.
If property is not found, may return JS_UNDEFINED unless throw_ref_error triggers an exception.

functions.name: JS_GetProperty
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper for JS_GetPropertyInternal using this_obj as receiver and not throwing on reference errors.
requirements: Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_GetPropertyStr
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetPropertyStr(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, const char *prop);
functions.description: Get a property by C string name.
requirements: prop must be a valid NUL-terminated property name.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_GetPropertyUint32
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetPropertyUint32(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, uint32_t idx);
functions.description: Get a property by array index (uint32).
requirements: Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_SetPropertyInternal
functions.signature: int JS_SetPropertyInternal(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, JSAtom prop, JSValue val, JSValueConst this_obj, int flags);
functions.description: Low-level property setter with explicit receiver and flags controlling behavior (e.g., throw in strict mode).
requirements: val is consumed on success or error; do not reuse; if needed, duplicate with JS_DupValue before passing.
Returns 1 on success (property set/created), 0 on failure according to JS semantics, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_SetProperty
functions.signature: int JS_SetProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop, JSValue val);
functions.description: Set a property by atom on an object, throwing on failure (JS_PROP_THROW).
requirements: val is consumed; duplicate if you need to retain it.
Returns 1 on success, -1 on exception, 0 if not set (rare due to THROW flag).

functions.name: JS_SetPropertyUint32
functions.signature: int JS_SetPropertyUint32(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, uint32_t idx, JSValue val);
functions.description: Set a property by array index on an object.

functions.name: JS_SetPropertyInt64
functions.signature: int JS_SetPropertyInt64(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, int64_t idx, JSValue val);
functions.description: Set a property by 64-bit index/key on an object.

functions.name: JS_SetPropertyStr
functions.signature: int JS_SetPropertyStr(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, const char *prop, JSValue val);
functions.description: Set a property by C string name on an object.
requirements: prop must be a valid NUL-terminated name.

functions.name: JS_HasProperty
functions.signature: int JS_HasProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop);
functions.description: Check if an object has a property (own or inherited).
requirements: Returns 1 if present, 0 if not, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_IsExtensible
functions.description: Check if an object is extensible.
requirements: Returns 1 if extensible, 0 if not, <0 on exception.

functions.name: JS_PreventExtensions
functions.description: Make an object non-extensible.

functions.name: JS_DeleteProperty
functions.signature: int JS_DeleteProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, JSAtom prop, int flags);
functions.description: Delete a property from an object with optional flags controlling behavior.
requirements: Returns 1 if property was deleted, 0 if not present or not deleted per semantics, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_SetPrototype
functions.signature: int JS_SetPrototype(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, JSValueConst proto_val);
functions.description: Set the [[Prototype]] of an object.
requirements: proto_val must be an object or JS_NULL.

functions.name: JS_GetPrototype
functions.description: Get the [[Prototype]] of an object or function value.
requirements: Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.
Return may be JS_NULL if no prototype; free with JS_FreeValue(ctx, v) if ref-counted.

functions.name: JS_GetOwnPropertyNames
functions.signature: int JS_GetOwnPropertyNames(JSContext *ctx, JSPropertyEnum **ptab, uint32_t *plen, JSValueConst obj, int flags);
functions.description: Enumerate own property keys of an object into a newly allocated table with count in *plen.
requirements: ptab and plen must be valid pointers; on success, *ptab must be freed with JS_FreePropertyEnum(ctx, *ptab, *plen).

functions.name: JS_FreePropertyEnum
functions.description: Free a property enumeration table returned by JS_GetOwnPropertyNames.
requirements: tab must be the pointer returned by JS_GetOwnPropertyNames for this context.
len must match the length returned.

functions.name: JS_GetOwnProperty
functions.signature: int JS_GetOwnProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSPropertyDescriptor *desc, JSValueConst obj, JSAtom prop);
functions.description: Get the property descriptor for an own property of an object.
requirements: desc may be NULL if only existence is needed (per exotic methods comment), but here function wants to fill desc; pass non-NULL to retrieve details.
Returns <0 on exception, 0 if not present, >0 if present (and desc filled).

functions.name: JS_Call
functions.signature: JSValue JS_Call(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst func_obj, JSValueConst this_obj, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Call a JS function with a given this and arguments.
requirements: func_obj must be a callable function; otherwise exception.
argv must point to at least argc arguments (or NULL if argc==0).
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_Invoke
functions.signature: JSValue JS_Invoke(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_val, JSAtom atom, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Invoke a method on an object by property atom name with arguments.
requirements: this_val should be an object; atom must name a callable property.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_CallConstructor
functions.signature: JSValue JS_CallConstructor(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst func_obj, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Call a constructor function with arguments (equivalent to new func(...)).
requirements: func_obj must be a constructor; otherwise exception.
Returns constructed object or JS_EXCEPTION on error.

functions.name: JS_CallConstructor2
functions.signature: JSValue JS_CallConstructor2(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst func_obj, JSValueConst new_target, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Call a constructor with an explicit new.target value.
requirements: new_target should be a constructor or function object.

functions.name: JS_DetectModule
functions.description: Heuristically detect if the given source text is an ES module. Input must be zero-terminated (input[input_len] = '\0').
requirements: input must be non-NULL and zero-terminated at input[input_len].
Returns non-zero if module detected, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: JS_Eval
functions.signature: JSValue JS_Eval(JSContext *ctx, const char *input, size_t input_len, const char *filename, int eval_flags);
functions.description: Compile (and optionally execute) JavaScript source. Supports flags for script/module, strict mode, compile-only, etc.
requirements: filename must be a valid C string (used for diagnostics).
eval_flags is a bitmask of JS_EVAL_* flags; JS_EVAL_FLAG_COMPILE_ONLY returns a function/module object.
Returns a JSValue (result, Promise if ASYNC) or JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check and free.

functions.name: JS_EvalThis
functions.signature: JSValue JS_EvalThis(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, const char *input, size_t input_len, const char *filename, int eval_flags);
functions.description: Same as JS_Eval but with an explicit this value for top-level execution.
requirements: this_obj is used as this binding.
input must be zero-terminated at input[input_len].
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_GetGlobalObject
functions.description: Get the global object for the context.
requirements: Returns a JS object value; must be freed with JS_FreeValue(ctx, v) when done if ref-counted.

functions.name: JS_IsInstanceOf
functions.signature: int JS_IsInstanceOf(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst val, JSValueConst obj);
functions.description: Test whether val is an instance of constructor obj (like val instanceof obj).
requirements: Returns 1 if true, 0 if false, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_DefineProperty
functions.signature: int JS_DefineProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop, JSValueConst val, JSValueConst getter, JSValueConst setter, int flags);
functions.description: Define a property with value/getter/setter and flags, similar to Object.defineProperty.
requirements: Flags combine JS_PROP_* and JS_PROP_HAS_* to indicate supplied fields.
Returns 0 on success (per QuickJS convention) or -1 on exception (note: QuickJS uses various conventions; caller must check for <0 as error).

functions.name: JS_DefinePropertyValue
functions.signature: int JS_DefinePropertyValue(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop, JSValue val, int flags);
functions.description: Define or set a property value with flags; consumes val.
requirements: val is consumed; duplicate first if needed.

functions.name: JS_DefinePropertyValueUint32
functions.signature: int JS_DefinePropertyValueUint32(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, uint32_t idx, JSValue val, int flags);
functions.description: Define or set a property by array index with flags; consumes val.

functions.name: JS_DefinePropertyValueStr
functions.signature: int JS_DefinePropertyValueStr(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, const char *prop, JSValue val, int flags);
functions.description: Define or set a property by C string name with flags; consumes val.
requirements: prop must be a NUL-terminated name.

functions.name: JS_DefinePropertyGetSet
functions.signature: int JS_DefinePropertyGetSet(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop, JSValue getter, JSValue setter, int flags);
functions.description: Define property accessor functions with flags; consumes getter/setter values.
requirements: getter and setter are consumed; pass JS_UNDEFINED if not provided.

functions.name: JS_SetOpaque
functions.description: Associate a host opaque pointer with a C-defined (native) object instance.
requirements: obj must be an object of a C-defined class with an opaque slot.
No ownership transfer implied; the embedder manages lifetime.

functions.name: JS_GetOpaque
functions.description: Retrieve the opaque pointer stored in a C-defined object if its class ID matches; otherwise return NULL.
requirements: class_id must be the expected class.
Safe to return NULL if mismatch or no opaque set.

functions.name: JS_GetOpaque2
functions.description: Same as JS_GetOpaque but throws a TypeError (exception) if obj is not an object of the expected class. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: Caller must check for exception if NULL is returned (JS_IsException on a separate operation).

functions.name: JS_GetAnyOpaque
functions.description: Retrieve the opaque pointer from a C-defined object along with its class ID.
requirements: obj must be an object with an opaque pointer.
class_id must be a valid pointer to receive the class ID.

functions.name: JS_ParseJSON
functions.signature: JSValue JS_ParseJSON(JSContext *ctx, const char *buf, size_t buf_len, const char *filename);
functions.description: Parse a JSON buffer (zero-terminated at buf[buf_len]) into a JS value. filename is used for diagnostics.
requirements: buf must be zero-terminated at buf[buf_len].
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_ParseJSON2
functions.signature: JSValue JS_ParseJSON2(JSContext *ctx, const char *buf, size_t buf_len, const char *filename, int flags);
functions.description: Parse JSON with optional flags (JS_PARSE_JSON_EXT to allow extensions).
requirements: buf must be zero-terminated at buf[buf_len].
flags is a bitmask of JS_PARSE_JSON_* values.

functions.name: JS_JSONStringify
functions.signature: JSValue JS_JSONStringify(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, JSValueConst replacer, JSValueConst space0);
functions.description: Stringify a JS value to JSON, optionally with a replacer and spacing.
requirements: Returns a JS string or JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check and free.

functions.name: JS_NewArrayBuffer
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewArrayBuffer(JSContext *ctx, uint8_t *buf, size_t len, JSFreeArrayBufferDataFunc *free_func, void *opaque, JS_BOOL is_shared);
functions.description: Create an ArrayBuffer that uses caller-provided memory and a callback to free it. Can create SharedArrayBuffer if is_shared is true.
requirements: buf must point to at least len bytes and remain valid until free_func is called by the engine.
free_func must be provided to release buf, unless special ownership rules apply (not documented); it will be called with rt, opaque, ptr.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_NewArrayBufferCopy
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewArrayBufferCopy(JSContext *ctx, const uint8_t *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Create a new ArrayBuffer whose contents are a copy of buf[0..len).
requirements: buf must point to at least len bytes (can be NULL if len==0).
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_DetachArrayBuffer
functions.description: Detach the underlying data from an ArrayBuffer object, making its views unusable.
requirements: obj must be an ArrayBuffer object.

functions.name: JS_GetArrayBuffer
functions.description: Get a pointer to the raw bytes of an (un-detached) ArrayBuffer and its size.
requirements: On success, *psize receives the size; returned pointer becomes invalid if the buffer is detached or GC’d; do not free it.

functions.name: JS_NewTypedArray
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewTypedArray(JSContext *ctx, int argc, JSValueConst *argv, JSTypedArrayEnum array_type);
functions.description: Create a new TypedArray of the given element type using arguments similar to JS constructors (length, buffer+offset+length, or from array).
requirements: argv must have at least argc items describing the constructor arguments.
array_type must be a valid JSTypedArrayEnum value.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_GetTypedArrayBuffer
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetTypedArrayBuffer(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, size_t *pbyte_offset, size_t *pbyte_length, size_t *pbytes_per_element);
functions.description: Extract the underlying ArrayBuffer from a TypedArray/DataView, along with byte offset, length, and bytes-per-element.
requirements: obj must be a TypedArray/DataView object.
Output pointers may be NULL if not needed; otherwise must be writable.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.
Returned JSValue is the ArrayBuffer; free with JS_FreeValue(ctx, v) if ref-counted.

functions.name: JS_SetSharedArrayBufferFunctions
functions.description: Provide host callbacks to allocate/free/duplicate shared memory backing for SharedArrayBuffer.
requirements: sf must point to valid function pointers and a stable opaque pointer for the lifetime they are used.

functions.name: JS_NewPromiseCapability
functions.description: Create a new Promise and fill resolving_funcs[0] and [1] with resolve and reject functions.
requirements: resolving_funcs must point to an array of at least two JSValue slots to receive functions; caller must free them when done.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_PromiseState
functions.description: Get the current state of a Promise (pending, fulfilled, rejected).
requirements: promise must be a Promise object; otherwise behavior may throw or return unspecified (not documented).

functions.name: JS_PromiseResult
functions.description: Get the fulfillment value or rejection reason of a settled Promise.
requirements: promise must be a Promise object and should be settled; otherwise may throw/return undefined.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_SetHostPromiseRejectionTracker
functions.description: Install a host callback that is notified of unhandled and handled Promise rejections.
requirements: cb may be NULL to clear; opaque is passed to the callback.

functions.name: JS_SetInterruptHandler
functions.description: Set a host interrupt handler that can request to interrupt JS execution (e.g., for timeouts).
requirements: cb may be NULL to clear; opaque passed to callback.
Handler should be fast and reentrant-safe.

functions.name: JS_SetCanBlock
functions.description: Inform the runtime whether it is allowed to block (enables Atomics.wait).

functions.name: JS_SetStripInfo
functions.description: Control stripping of source and debug info from compiled code (JS_STRIP_SOURCE/JS_STRIP_DEBUG).
requirements: flags is a bitmask of JS_STRIP_* values.

functions.name: JS_GetStripInfo
functions.description: Get the current strip-info flags for the runtime.

functions.name: JS_SetIsHTMLDDA
functions.description: Set the [IsHTMLDDA] internal slot on an object (special web-compat behavior).

functions.name: JS_SetModuleLoaderFunc
functions.description: Install host callbacks for module specifier normalization and module loading. Attributes not supported in this variant.
requirements: module_normalize may be NULL to use default normalizer.
module_loader must be provided to load modules; opaque is passed through.

functions.name: JS_SetModuleLoaderFunc2
functions.signature: void JS_SetModuleLoaderFunc2(JSRuntime *rt, JSModuleNormalizeFunc *module_normalize, JSModuleLoaderFunc2 *module_loader, JSModuleCheckSupportedImportAttributes *module_check_attrs, void *opaque);
functions.description: Install host callbacks for module normalization, loading with attributes, and optional attribute validation.
requirements: module_normalize may be NULL to use default.
module_loader must be provided for loading; attributes are provided.
module_check_attrs may be NULL to skip attribute checking.

functions.name: JS_GetImportMeta
functions.description: Return the import.meta object for a module.
requirements: m must be a valid module pointer.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_GetModuleName
functions.description: Return the module’s name as an atom.
requirements: m must be a valid module pointer.

functions.name: JS_GetModuleNamespace
functions.description: Return the module’s namespace object.
requirements: Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_EnqueueJob
functions.signature: int JS_EnqueueJob(JSContext *ctx, JSJobFunc *job_func, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Schedule a microtask/job to run later in the job queue.
requirements: job_func must be a valid function pointer; it will be called with argv.
argv must have at least argc items (may be NULL if argc==0).

functions.name: JS_IsJobPending
functions.description: Return whether there are pending jobs in the job queue.

functions.name: JS_ExecutePendingJob
functions.description: Execute one pending job from the job queue. Optionally returns the context used via pctx.
requirements: pctx may be NULL; if non-NULL must point to a JSContext* location.
Returns <0 on exception, 0 if no job was executed, >0 if a job ran.

functions.name: JS_WriteObject
functions.signature: uint8_t *JS_WriteObject(JSContext *ctx, size_t *psize, JSValueConst obj, int flags);
functions.description: Serialize an object (function/module allowed with flags) to a binary buffer. Returns malloc’d buffer and size in *psize.
requirements: psize must be a valid pointer to receive size.
obj must be serializable given flags (JS_WRITE_OBJ_*).
Returns NULL on error; caller must check.
Caller must free the buffer with js_free(ctx, ptr).

functions.name: JS_WriteObject2
functions.signature: uint8_t *JS_WriteObject2(JSContext *ctx, size_t *psize, JSValueConst obj, int flags, uint8_t ***psab_tab, size_t *psab_tab_len);
functions.description: Serialize an object with optional extraction of SharedArrayBuffer references into an array, returning the main buffer and the SAB table.
requirements: psab_tab and psab_tab_len may be NULL if SAB export not required; otherwise must be writable and subsequently freed per QuickJS rules (free with js_free on inner pointers).
Returns NULL on error; caller must free returned buffers with js_free(ctx, ...).

functions.name: JS_ReadObject
functions.signature: JSValue JS_ReadObject(JSContext *ctx, const uint8_t *buf, size_t buf_len, int flags);
functions.description: Deserialize an object/function/module from a binary buffer produced by JS_WriteObject*.
requirements: buf must point to buf_len bytes; if JS_READ_OBJ_ROM_DATA is set, buf must remain valid for the lifetime of the resulting object graph.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_EvalFunction
functions.description: Instantiate and evaluate a compiled function or module object previously produced by JS_Eval with COMPILE_ONLY or JS_ReadObject.
requirements: fun_obj must be a function/module bytecode object.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.
fun_obj is consumed by evaluation or must be managed by caller accordingly (unspecified).

functions.name: JS_ResolveModule
functions.description: Load/resolve dependencies of a module object previously read via JS_ReadObject.
requirements: obj must be a module object.

functions.name: JS_GetScriptOrModuleName
functions.description: Return the script or module name (as atom) from the call stack, for worker support.
requirements: n_stack_levels selects how many frames up to inspect.

functions.name: JS_LoadModule
functions.signature: JSValue JS_LoadModule(JSContext *ctx, const char *basename, const char *filename);
functions.description: Load a module from a file for os.Worker() support, returning a module object.
requirements: basename and filename must be valid C strings.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_NewCFunction2
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewCFunction2(JSContext *ctx, JSCFunction *func, const char *name, int length, JSCFunctionEnum cproto, int magic);
functions.description: Create a new JS function object wrapping a C function with a specified calling convention, name, length, and magic value.
requirements: func must match cproto calling convention.
name must be a NUL-terminated string.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_NewCFunctionData
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewCFunctionData(JSContext *ctx, JSCFunctionData *func, int length, int magic, int data_len, JSValueConst *data);
functions.description: Create a new C function with embedded constant data array accessible by the function.
requirements: func must be a valid function pointer.
If data_len > 0, data must point to at least data_len values.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_NewCFunction
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewCFunction(JSContext *ctx, JSCFunction *func, const char *name, int length);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper to create a generic C function with the given name and length.
requirements: func must match the generic signature.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_NewCFunctionMagic
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewCFunctionMagic(JSContext *ctx, JSCFunctionMagic *func, const char *name, int length, JSCFunctionEnum cproto, int magic);
functions.description: Create a C function with a magic value and specified calling convention; avoids -Wcast-function-type by using a union.
requirements: func must match the cproto variant with magic.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_SetConstructor
functions.signature: int JS_SetConstructor(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst func_obj, JSValueConst proto);
functions.description: Set a function’s prototype property and mark it as a constructor for objects with the given prototype.
requirements: func_obj must be a function object.
proto must be an object (the prototype).

functions.name: JS_SetPropertyFunctionList
functions.signature: int JS_SetPropertyFunctionList(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, const JSCFunctionListEntry *tab, int len);
functions.description: Define a list of properties, methods, accessors, and constants on an object from a table.
requirements: tab must point to an array of len entries describing properties.

functions.name: JS_NewCModule
functions.description: Create a new C module with the given name and an initialization function that defines its exports.
requirements: name_str must be a unique module name string.
func must be a valid init function.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check.

functions.name: JS_AddModuleExport
functions.description: Declare a single export name for a C module (before instantiation).
requirements: m must be the module returned by JS_NewCModule and not yet instantiated.
name_str must be a valid export name.

functions.name: JS_AddModuleExportList
functions.signature: int JS_AddModuleExportList(JSContext *ctx, JSModuleDef *m, const JSCFunctionListEntry *tab, int len);
functions.description: Declare multiple exports for a C module from a function list table (before instantiation).
requirements: m must be not yet instantiated.
tab must be a valid array of len entries.

functions.name: JS_SetModuleExport
functions.signature: int JS_SetModuleExport(JSContext *ctx, JSModuleDef *m, const char *export_name, JSValue val);
functions.description: Set the value of a previously-declared module export (after instantiation). Consumes val.
requirements: export_name must refer to a declared export name.
val is consumed; do not reuse unless duplicated.

functions.name: JS_SetModuleExportList
functions.signature: int JS_SetModuleExportList(JSContext *ctx, JSModuleDef *m, const JSCFunctionListEntry *tab, int len);
functions.description: Set multiple exports for a C module from a property/function list (after instantiation).
requirements: tab must be valid with len entries.

functions.name: JS_SetModulePrivateValue
functions.description: Associate a JSValue as private data to a C module; ownership transfers to the module.
requirements: m must be valid C module.
val is consumed; do not free after passing.

functions.name: JS_GetModulePrivateValue
functions.description: Retrieve the JSValue previously stored as a module’s private value.
requirements: Returned value follows normal JSValue lifetime; free with JS_FreeValue(ctx, v) when done.

functions.name: JS_PrintValueSetDefaultOptions
functions.description: Initialize a JSPrintValueOptions struct with default settings.
requirements: options must be a valid writable pointer.

functions.name: JS_PrintValueRT
functions.signature: void JS_PrintValueRT(JSRuntime *rt, JSPrintValueWrite *write_func, void *write_opaque, JSValueConst val, const JSPrintValueOptions *options);
functions.description: Render a human-readable representation of a value using a write callback at the runtime level (no context needed).
requirements: write_func must not be NULL and must handle the provided buffers until return.
options may be NULL to use defaults (if caller initialized); otherwise must point to a valid options struct.

functions.name: JS_PrintValue
functions.signature: void JS_PrintValue(JSContext *ctx, JSPrintValueWrite *write_func, void *write_opaque, JSValueConst val, const JSPrintValueOptions *options);
functions.description: Render a human-readable representation of a value using a write callback, with a context.
requirements: write_func must be non-NULL and able to handle writes.
options may be NULL or point to a valid struct.

functions.name: js_init_module_std
functions.description: Initialize and return the built-in 'std' C module (QuickJS libc).
requirements: module_name must match the module’s registration name.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check.

functions.name: js_init_module_os
functions.description: Initialize and return the built-in 'os' C module (QuickJS libc).
requirements: module_name must match the module’s registration name.

functions.name: js_std_add_helpers
functions.description: Add standard helper functions and objects to a context (from QuickJS libc), using process argv for configuration.
requirements: argv must point to at least argc pointers if argc>0.

functions.name: js_std_loop
functions.description: Run the standard event loop processing pending jobs and I/O (QuickJS libc).

functions.name: js_std_await
functions.description: Helper to synchronously await a Promise-like object in the standard library environment.
requirements: obj is consumed or used; returns a value or throws JS_EXCEPTION; caller must check.

functions.name: js_std_init_handlers
functions.description: Install standard library handlers (e.g., promise rejection tracker, interrupt) on a runtime.

functions.name: js_std_free_handlers
functions.description: Remove/free handlers installed by js_std_init_handlers from a runtime.

functions.name: js_std_dump_error
functions.description: Print the current pending exception (if any) to stderr using libc helpers.
requirements: Should be called after an operation that returned JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: js_load_file
functions.description: Load a file from disk into a newly allocated buffer; return pointer and set its length.
requirements: filename must be a valid path.
pbuf_len must be a valid pointer to receive size.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check.
Free the returned buffer with js_free(ctx, ptr).

functions.name: js_module_set_import_meta
functions.signature: int js_module_set_import_meta(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst func_val, JS_BOOL use_realpath, JS_BOOL is_main);
functions.description: Set import.meta properties for a module function value (std lib helper).
requirements: func_val must be a module function value.
use_realpath and is_main control metadata fields.

functions.name: js_module_test_json
functions.description: Test whether import attributes indicate a JSON module (std lib helper).
requirements: attributes must be an object or appropriate value.
Returns 0/1 typical, -1 on exception (exact semantics not documented).

functions.name: js_module_check_attributes
functions.description: Validate module import attributes (std lib helper) for host loader integration.
requirements: attributes must be an attributes object/value.

functions.name: js_module_loader
functions.signature: JSModuleDef *js_module_loader(JSContext *ctx, const char *module_name, void *opaque, JSValueConst attributes);
functions.description: Default module loader implementation for std/libc that loads modules by name with attributes.
requirements: module_name must be a valid module specifier.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check.

functions.name: js_std_eval_binary
functions.signature: void js_std_eval_binary(JSContext *ctx, const uint8_t *buf, size_t buf_len, int flags);
functions.description: Evaluate a precompiled binary (bytecode) buffer with optional flags (std lib helper).
requirements: buf must point to buf_len bytes representing a QuickJS bytecode object.
flags should be JS_READ_OBJ_* or writer/reader compatible flags.

functions.name: js_std_eval_binary_json_module

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets a generic C string used by many QuickJS APIs in the stubs.
# It returns a bytes object that the fuzzing framework will feed into FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
# and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. We focus on producing valid, interesting NUL-terminated
# text without embedded NULs (the framework will handle termination), covering:
# - JavaScript snippets for JS_Eval/JS_EvalThis (scripts/modules, strict, async)
# - JSON texts for JS_ParseJSON/ParseJSON2
# - Property names and atoms (identifiers, unicode, numeric indices, symbols-like)
# - Filenames and module names
# - Error message strings (for JS_Throw* formatting)
#
# The output size is capped to <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_OUT = 4096

# Some interesting JS/JSON/code/name samples
JS_SNIPPETS = [
    "",  # empty
    "42",
    "'hello'",
    "({a:1,b:2})",
    "[1,2,3,4]",
    "function f(a,b){return a+b} f(1,2)",
    "(() => 123)()",
    "var x=1; x",
    "let x=1; x",
    "const x=1; x",
    "try{throw new Error('e')}catch(e){e.message}",
    "class C{constructor(x){this.x=x}} new C(5).x",
    "async function a(){return 7} a().then(v=>v)",
    "await (async()=>5)()",  # useful when in module/await contexts
    "import('data:text/javascript,export default 1').then(m=>m.default)",
    "if (this) { 1 } else { 0 }",
    "for (let i=0;i<3;i++){}; 0",
    "let o={}; Object.defineProperty(o,'p',{get(){return 1}}); o.p",
    "let a=new Uint8Array(4); a[0]=1; a.length",
]

MODULE_SNIPPETS = [
    "export default 42;",
    "export const x=1; export function f(){return x}; f()",
    "import x from 'data:text/javascript,export default 5'; export {x};",
]

JSON_SAMPLES = [
    "null",
    "true",
    "false",
    "0",
    "12345",
    "\"str\"",
    "[]",
    "[1,2,3]",
    "{}",
    "{\"a\":1,\"b\":[2,3],\"c\":{\"d\":4}}",
    "{\"type\":\"json\"}",
]

# Property names / atoms
PROP_NAMES = [
    "x", "y", "p", "length", "constructor", "prototype", "toString",
    "__proto__", "δ", "こんにちは", "😀", "0", "123", "a_b", "$", "_",
]

# File/module-ish names
FILENAMES = [
    "fuzz_eval.js", "fuzz_eval_this.js", "fuzz.json", "fuzz2.json",
    "module.mjs", "index.js", "a/b/c.js", "\\\\network\\share\\file.js",
    "./relative/path.js", "/abs/path/script.js",
]

ERROR_MESSAGES = [
    "syntax error near unexpected token",
    "Type mismatch: expected number",
    "Reference not found",
    "Range exceeded",
    "Internal failure occurred",
]

IDENT_START = string.ascii_letters + "$_"
IDENT_CONT = IDENT_START + string.digits

def rand_identifier(rnd: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=20) -> str:
    n = rnd.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = rnd.choice(IDENT_START)
    for _ in range(n-1):
        s += rnd.choice(IDENT_CONT)
    return s

def rand_unicode_prop(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # mix BMP and some higher code points represented in UTF-8
    parts = [
        "α", "β", "γ", "Ω", "漢字", "🙂", "🚀", "ñ", "ç",
        rand_identifier(rnd),
        str(rnd.randint(0, 100000)),
    ]
    return rnd.choice(parts)

def build_js_source(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Randomly choose between script or module-like forms and add directives/comments
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        body = rnd.choice(JS_SNIPPETS)
    else:
        body = rnd.choice(MODULE_SNIPPETS)
    pre = []
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        pre.append("'use strict';")
    if rnd.random() < 0.2:
        pre.append("// fuzz header")
    return "\n".join(pre + [body])

def build_json(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        return rnd.choice(JSON_SAMPLES)
    # generate an object with random properties
    obj = {}
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(0, 5)):
        k = rand_unicode_prop(rnd)
        # ensure JSON-safe key (no control chars). JSON module in QuickJS expects valid JSON
        obj[k] = rnd.choice([None, True, False, rnd.randint(-1000, 1000), rnd.random(), rnd.choice(["str", "json", "val"])])
    # Build JSON manually via repr-like but ensuring validity by using Python's json
    import json as _json
    return _json.dumps(obj)

def build_property_name(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        return rnd.choice(PROP_NAMES)
    return rand_unicode_prop(rnd)

def build_filename(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        return rnd.choice(FILENAMES)
    # Compose a plausible filename/module spec
    base = rand_identifier(rnd, 1, 8)
    ext = rnd.choice([".js", ".mjs", ".json", ""]) if rnd.random() < 0.9 else ""
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        return base + ext
    # path-like
    parts = [rand_identifier(rnd, 1, 6) for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3))]
    return "/".join(parts + [base + ext])

def build_error_message(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    msg = rnd.choice(ERROR_MESSAGES)
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        msg += f" at {build_filename(rnd)}:{rnd.randint(1,200)}:{rnd.randint(1,120)}"
    return msg

def assemble_pool(rnd: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    pool: List[str] = []
    # Include multiple of each category to supply different FUZZ_PARAM_STR call sites
    pool.append(build_js_source(rnd))
    pool.append(build_json(rnd))
    pool.append(build_property_name(rnd))
    pool.append(build_filename(rnd))
    pool.append(build_error_message(rnd))
    # Add a few extras
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(2, 6)):
        pool.append(build_property_name(rnd))
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3)):
        pool.append(build_js_source(rnd))
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3)):
        pool.append(build_json(rnd))
    # Ensure some small strings for edge cases
    pool.extend(["a", "", "0", "json", "type"])  # small/empty, common keys
    return pool


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    pool = assemble_pool(rnd)

    # Join entries with newlines; the harness will split requests across FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    # calls, but providing a buffer containing multiple valid strings increases chance
    # of covering various sites early.
    joined = "\n".join(pool)

    # Ensure no embedded NULs and cap size
    data = joined.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass')
    if len(data) > MAX_OUT:
        data = data[:MAX_OUT]
        # avoid truncating inside a multi-byte sequence creating invalid UTF-8 is fine for atoms,
        # but most APIs accept arbitrary bytes via c_str. Keep as-is.

    return data

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for binary string inputs tailored to QuickJS fuzz stubs that expect:
# - Arbitrary byte sequences for JS_NewStringLen / JS_NewAtomLen / JS_NewArrayBufferCopy
# - Zero-terminated buffers with explicit input_len at buf[input_len] for JS_Eval/ParseJSON/DetectModule
# - Filenames for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME that the harness will map to fuzz data
# Our output is a single bytes buffer consumed by the fuzzer to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME.
# Strategy:
#  - Construct a concatenation of multiple length-prefixed binary payloads so the harness
#    can slice different FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls from the same buffer deterministically.
#  - Include a mix of interesting JavaScript/JSON/module-like snippets and raw binary to
#    drive different code paths while remaining valid when used as length-delimited strings.
#  - Ensure embedded NULs appear only within payload bodies; stubs that require zero-termination
#    explicitly append a NUL themselves, so our raw data can be arbitrary.
#  - Also embed some path-like strings for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME usage.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

JS_SNIPPETS = [
    b"",  # empty
    b"42",
    b"'hello'",
    b"\"world\"",
    b"(function(a,b){return a+b;})(1,2)",
    b"let x=1/0,y=-0,z=NaN;({x,y,z})",
    b"class A{}; new A();",
    b"import.meta",
    b"export default 123",  # module-ish
    b"async function f(){return 5}; f().then(()=>0)",
    b"try{throw new Error('e')}catch(e){e.toString()}",
    b"'\u{1F600}'",  # Unicode codepoint
]

JSON_SNIPPETS = [
    b"{}",
    b"[]",
    b"{\"a\":1,\"b\":[1,2,3]}",
    b"{\"str\":\"hello\",\"n\":-0,\"nan\":null}",
    b"[true,false,null,\"x\",123]",
]

MODULE_LIKE = [
    b"import x from 'm'; export {x};",
    b"export const v=1; export function f(){}",
    b"import('dyn')",
]

FILENAMES = [
    b"/tmp/fuzz.js",
    b"/tmp/fuzz.json",
    b"/tmp/mod.mjs",
    b"C:\\fuzz\\in.txt",
    b"relative/path/file.js",
]

BINARY_PATTERNS = [
    # Small binary blobs including NULs
    b"\x00",
    b"\x00\x01\x02\x03\x04\xff\x80\x7f",
    os.urandom(16),
]

UNICODE_BYTES = [
    "😀🐍漢字ñéâ€”.".encode("utf-8"),
    "\u0000\u0001A\u07FF\u0800\uFFFF".encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"),
]

# Helper to build a length-prefixed segment: [u16 len][bytes]
# Using little-endian 16-bit lengths to keep total < 4096.

def _lp(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    if len(b) > 0xFFFF:
        b = b[:0xFFFF]
    return struct.pack('<H', len(b)) + b


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _mix_buffers(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    out: List[bytes] = []
    # Include several JS source candidates (used by JS_Eval/This and detection)
    js_pool = JS_SNIPPETS + MODULE_LIKE
    rng.shuffle(js_pool)
    for s in js_pool[:rng.randint(3, 6)]:
        out.append(s)

    # Include JSON candidates for JS_ParseJSON/2
    jpool = JSON_SNIPPETS[:]
    rng.shuffle(jpool)
    for s in jpool[:rng.randint(2, 4)]:
        out.append(s)

    # Include raw binary for string/atom/arraybuffer APIs
    out.extend(BINARY_PATTERNS)
    out.extend(UNICODE_BYTES)

    # Add some random-length arbitrary binary chunks, some containing NULs
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        n = rng.randint(0, 64)
        b = _rand_bytes(rng, n)
        # Occasionally sprinkle a NUL
        if n and rng.random() < 0.5:
            i = rng.randrange(n)
            b = b[:i] + b"\x00" + b[i+1:]
        out.append(b)

    # Add filename-like strings
    out.extend(FILENAMES)

    # Add some atoms/identifiers typical for property names
    out.extend([b"a", b"length", b"constructor", b"toString", b"valueOf", b"prototype"])

    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    segments = _mix_buffers(rng)

    # Randomly permute and possibly duplicate a few to ensure variety across FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    rng.shuffle(segments)
    dup_count = rng.randint(0, 4)
    for _ in range(dup_count):
        if segments:
            segments.insert(rng.randrange(len(segments)+1), rng.choice(segments))

    # Serialize as a simple container format:
    # [u16 segment_count][ [u16 len][bytes] ... ]
    # The harness can be adapted to read sequential strings. Our fuzzer stubs typically
    # call FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times; this format allows deterministic extraction.
    buf = bytearray()
    # We'll cap total to MAX_TOTAL bytes
    temp = bytearray()
    serialized: List[bytes] = []
    for seg in segments:
        part = _lp(seg)
        if 2 + len(temp) + len(part) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        serialized.append(part)
        temp.extend(part)
    count = len(serialized)
    buf.extend(struct.pack('<H', count))
    for part in serialized:
        buf.extend(part)

    # If buffer is still small, pad with a few random segments to reach some entropy
    while len(buf) < min(MAX_TOTAL, 512):
        rnd = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 32))
        part = _lp(rnd)
        if len(buf) + len(part) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        buf.extend(part)

    return bytes(buf)
